stretch_notes: Around 2014, Amazon began building an AI tool to automatically screen job applicants' resumes. However, the model was trained on 10 years of historical hiring data, a period during which the tech industry was overwhelmingly male. Consequently, the AI taught itself that male candidates were preferable. It actively penalized resumes that included the word "women's" and downgraded graduates from two all-women's colleges. Despite engineers' attempts to manually edit the algorithm to be neutral, they couldn't guarantee it wouldn't find other proxy variables for gender. Amazon ultimately scrapped the project in 2018, demonstrating how AI can scale and automate historical human prejudices.
